subject: bauhausBird
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: songbird on a branch.
Style: Bauhaus primary-colour geometry.
reasoning:
I'm planning a small songbird perched on a branch in Bauhaus primary-colour geometric style, keeping the piece modestly sized but polished. I'm working out real-world scale—bird around 12-14cm with the branch positioned so the model rests properly at ground level, feet gripping the branch.

I'm sketching the colour palette: blue body, yellow belly, red head and wings, black tail, with a black branch accented by yellow disc ornaments at the ends. I'm also planning a simple rig with root, body, neck, head, jaw, tail, wing, and leg joints, favoring straightforward parts and sweeps over risky complex geometry to keep things stable, with the model oriented facing +Z and the body centered just above the branch.

Default dir is along Y, so for cones like the tail and beak I'll use [0,0,1] to point them forward. Going with the Bauhaus palette (red, yellow, blue, black, cream white) I'm shaping the beak as a small yellow pyramid-like cone on top with a flatter black lower jaw beneath it.

For the head I'm placing a red sphere with white disc eyes and black pupils positioned outward on each side, using thin cylinders for the disc thickness, plus a small tilted black triangular crest cone on top. The body becomes a blue ellipsoid with a yellow belly ellipsoid offset underneath and forward, and I'm adding a breast circle detail.

Working out the belly ellipsoid's exact offsets so it pokes out below and at the front of the body while staying tucked in at the sides, then shaping the folded wings as thin red ellipsoids angled against the body with black triangular wing tips.

Now I'm defining the tail: a black angled box for the main tail section attached near the back, plus a small red square tip piece at the end, both mounted on tail joints.

Positioning legs and toes gripping a horizontal branch along the X axis, with the bird perched sideways facing forward and toes wrapping over the top of the branch.

I'm figuring out the Bauhaus color accents on the branch ends, and considering whether to add small support blocks underneath to raise it off the floor rather than letting it rest flush on the ground.

Defining joint hierarchy...

Now I'm settling on the color scheme: red head with a white cheek disc and black pupil for a Bauhaus look, blue body, and considering yellow or red for the wings with a white bar and black tips. I'm also placing a small yellow cone beak on the head.

Setting the lower beak black against the red head, then placing a small black crest cone at the top of the head angled slightly back. Now I'm working out eye placement — white disc cylinders embedded into the sides of the head sphere, positioned using direction vectors scaled by the head radius so they sit flush on the surface.

Adding black pupils slightly outside the eye discs, then designing a red circular emblem on the belly's front surface, positioned and angled to sit flush against the yellow belly ellipsoid.

I'm thinking through a helper function for building body parts with shared shading and bone attachments, planning to keep everything rigged to a single root joint with hips as a child so static elements like the chest emblem move naturally with the bird.
